units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
D'y' think they'll be able to get that done before I buy the house--or rather the abbey? They're both abbeys.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: putting that aside rather impatiently.
Oh, well, let us talk sense, Mr Malone. You must feel that we haven't been talking sense so far.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: I can't say I do. I mean all I say.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: Then you don't know Hector as I do. He is romantic and faddy--he gets it from you, I fancy--and he wants a certain sort of wife to take care of him. Not a faddy sort of person, you know.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Somebody like you, perhaps?
units.name: MALONE

units.text: quietly.
Well, yes. But you cannot very well ask me to undertake this with absolutely no means of keeping up his position.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: alarmed.
Stop a bit, stop a bit. Where are we getting to? I'm not aware that I'm asking you to undertake anything.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: Of course, Mr Malone, you can make it very difficult for me to speak to you if you choose to misunderstand me.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: half bewildered.
I don't wish to take any unfair advantage; but we seem to have got off the straight track somehow.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: Straker, with the air of a man who has been making haste, opens the little gate, and admits Hector, who, snorting with indignation, comes upon the lawn, and is making for his father when Violet, greatly dismayed, springs up and intercepts him.
Straker doer not wait; at least he does not remain visibly within earshot.
Oh, how unlucky! Now please, Hector, say nothing. Go away until I have finished speaking to your father.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: inexorably.
No, Violet: I mean to have this thing out, right away.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: He puts her aside; passes her by; and faces his father, whose cheeks darken as his Irish blood begins to simmer.
Dad: you've not played this hand straight.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: Hwat d'y'mean?
units.name: MALONE

units.text: You've opened a letter addressed to me. You've impersonated me and stolen a march on this lady. That's dishonorable.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: threateningly.
Now you take care what you're saying, Hector. Take care, I tell you.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: I have taken care. I am taking care. I'm taking care of my honor and my position in English society.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: hotly.
Your position has been got by my money: do you know that?
units.name: MALONE

units.text: Well, you've just spoiled it all by opening that letter. A letter from an English lady, not addressed to you--a confidential letter! a delicate letter! a private letter opened by my father! That's a sort of thing a man can't struggle against in England. The sooner we go back together the better.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: He appeals mutely to the heavens to witness the shame and anguish of two outcasts.
snubbing him with an instinctive dislike for scene making.
Don't be unreasonable, Hector. It was quite natural of Mr Malone to open my letter: his name was on the envelope.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: There! You've no common sense, Hector. I thank you, Miss Robinson.
units.name: MALONE

units.text: I thank you, too. It's very kind of you. My father knows no better.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: furiously clenching his fists.
Hector--
units.name: MALONE

units.text: with undaunted moral force.
Oh, it's no use hectoring me. A private letter's a private letter, dad: you can't get over that.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: MALONE [raising his voice] I won't be talked back to by you, d'y' hear?
Ssh! please, please. Here they all come.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Father and son, checked, glare mutely at one another as Tanner comes in through the little gate with Ramsden, followed by Octavius and Ann.
Back already!
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: The Alhambra is not open this afternoon.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: What a sell!
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Tanner passes on, and presently finds himself between Hector and a strange elder, both apparently on the verge of personal combat.
He looks from one to the other for an explanation.
They sulkily avoid his eye, and nurse their wrath in silence.
Is it wise for you to be out in the sunshine with such a headache, Violet?
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: Have you recovered too, Malone?
units.name: TANNER
